- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.2) and price is rising, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven volatility.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals (e.g., +1, –1, +1), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next 3–5 days to catch momentum.
